theorem.statement: If an anchor pair (c,f) is exact-channel representable, then c and f are nonadjacent and have exactly one common neighbor z. Conversely, if cf is a nonedge, N(c) intersect N(f)={z}, and the unique fixed-triple reachability instance (z,c,f) is feasible, then (c,f) is exact-channel representable.

necessity: Every valid exact-channel representation requires cz,zf in E, hence z belongs to N(c) intersect N(f).
The sealed fixed-triple necessary prefilter gives (N(c) intersect N(f))\{z}=empty.
The sealed prefilter also gives cf notin E.
unique_hub.conclusion: The hub of a representable anchor pair is unique and graph-canonical.

converse: If cf is a nonedge and N(c) intersect N(f)={z}, there is exactly one eligible hub candidate.
Run the unique fixed-triple implication-reachability test for (z,c,f).
If Reach_D(R0) intersect L0 is empty, the fixed-triple theorem returns an exact-channel decomposition.
If the reachability test fails, no exact-channel decomposition exists for the anchor pair because no alternative hub exists.

pair_level_characterization.formula: (c,f) representable iff [cf notin E] AND [N(c) intersect N(f)={z} for a unique z] AND [Reach_{D_{z,c,f}}(R0) intersect L0=empty].
canonical_objects: canonical ports and channel graph for chosen canonical partition

representation_freedom_cleanup.PARTITION_FREEDOM: Exactly the distributive lattice of successor-closed implication solutions.
representation_freedom_cleanup.PARTITION_OPTIMIZATION_FOR_CAPACITY: UNNECESSARY because nu(X) is invariant across the lattice.
representation_freedom_cleanup.remaining_geometry: Only partition/lattice geometry remains after anchors are fixed.

algorithm: Enumerate anchor pairs (c,f), ordered or unordered according to the application convention.
Reject immediately if cf is an edge.
Continue only if the intersection is a singleton {z}.
Build the single implication graph D_{z,c,f}.
Accept iff R_min intersect L0 is empty.
On acceptance output the unique hub z, canonical R_min decomposition, R_max bound, canonical ports, and X.

complexity.simple_common_neighbor_scan: O(n) per anchor pair with an adjacency-matrix/bitset-compatible representation.
complexity.note: More output-sensitive wedge/common-neighbor counting implementations may improve constants or sparse-graph behavior, but are not needed for polynomiality.

capacity_pipeline.canonical_route: (c,f) -> unique z -> one reachability lattice -> canonical R_min -> canonical X -> nu(X)=rho_G(c,f).
capacity_pipeline.consequence: There is neither hub optimization nor partition optimization for fixed-anchor capacity.

positive: singleton common-neighbor certificate N(c) intersect N(f)={z}
negative_pair_level: at least two common neighbors; OR
unique common neighbor z plus forced-R to forced-L implication path certifying fixed-triple infeasibility

exhaustive_small_graph_sanity_check.authority: SANITY_CHECK_ONLY; theorem authority is the analytic implication from the sealed prefilter plus the fixed-triple reachability theorem.

relation_to_prior_invariance_theorem.statement: The prior theorem that matching capacity is invariant across different hubs for the same anchor pair remains formally correct.
relation_to_prior_invariance_theorem.sharpening: For the pure exact-channel interface, there cannot be two feasible hubs for one representable anchor pair; the cross-hub part is therefore vacuous. Nontrivial invariance remains across the partition lattice for the unique hub.
